segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין חַיָּיבִין עַל שְׁמִיעַת קוֹל, וְעַל בִּיטּוּי שְׂפָתַיִם, וְעַל טוּמְאַת מִקְדָּשׁ וְקָדָשָׁיו. וְהַנָּשִׂיא כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶם, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: הַנָּשִׂיא חַיָּיב בְּכוּלָּן חוּץ מִשְּׁמִיעַת הַקּוֹל, שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ לֹא דָּן וְלֹא דָּנִין אוֹתוֹ [לֹא מֵעִיד וְלֹא מְעִידִין אוֹתוֹ].
segments.en: «MISHNA:» The court «is not liable for» issuing a ruling with regard to «hearing of a voice,» i.e., a false oath of testimony taken by a witness who refuses to testify on behalf of a litigant who demands that he testify, «or for an utterance of the lips,» i.e., a false oath stated about some matter, «or for the defiling of» the «Temple or its sacrificial» foods. «And the» status of the «king is like» that of the court, and he is exempt from bringing an offering in those cases; this is «the statement of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili. Rabbi Akiva says: The king is liable in all of» those cases «except for» the case of «hearing of a voice,» and even in that case, his exemption is not intrinsic to the mitzva. Rather, it is for technical reasons, «as the king neither judges» others «nor» do others «judge him; he does not testify nor» do others «testify against him.» Therefore, a demand that he testify is not applicable.
